verdicts.reason: The docstring of get_failure_reason literally reads "Builds a humam readible string from a list of failed check-ins." — two misspellings, carried into the newly added file.

The queryset is sliced with previous_checkins[:failure_issue_threshold] and only the presence of an OK status short-circuits; a monitor whose entire history is one failing check-in yields a 1-element list, no OK is found, and MonitorStatus.ERROR + MonitorIncident are created despite a threshold of N. tests/sentry/monitors/logic/test_mark_failed.py::test_mark_failed_issue_threshold always seeds an OK check-in first, so this case is untested.
Same typo, correctly attributed to get_failure_reason's docstring: "humam readible" instead of "human readable".

Neither try_incident_threshold nor create_incident_occurrence has a docstring, and both perform heavy side effects (monitor_env.save, MonitorIncident.objects.get_or_create, produce_occurrence_to_kafka, monitor_environment_failed.send). The only prose describing that behaviour stayed behind on mark_failed in mark_failed.py:19-27 and was not restated in the extracted modules.
SINGULAR_HUMAN_FAILURE_MAP only contains "An error/A missed/A timeout check-in was detected"; the docstring's third example "A failed check-in was detected" is a string the function can never return.

Inside this checkout nothing references mark_failed_threshold, create_issue_platform_occurrence, or a SimpleCheckIn imported from mark_failed (the only create_issue_platform_occurrence hits are the unrelated uptime module). Settling it for private dependents such as getsentry needs a grep of a repository I do not have.

Statically the tests should be unaffected — they import only mark_failed and patch sentry.issues.producer.produce_occurrence_to_kafka at its source, which still resolves because create_incident_occurrence imports it inside the function body. Confirming an end-to-end pass needs postgres/kafka/redis, which I cannot run.

The premise is false: previous_checkins holds SimpleCheckIn dicts with only id/date_added/status (src/sentry/monitors/types.py:105-110), while create_incident_occurrence needs failed_checkin.monitor_environment and failed_checkin.trace_id, so the MonitorCheckIn.objects.filter(id__in=...) fetch is required, not redundant.
The comment reads "within the threshold of / commits" at exactly line 51; the loop below inspects check-in statuses, so "commits" is a stray word.
Same defect as c002 stated as the remedy: nothing checks len(previous_checkins) == failure_issue_threshold after the slice, so a short history opens an incident early.

config = monitor.config.copy() is mutated with the schedule_type display value, then the returned dict uses monitor_environment.monitor.config — the shallow copy is discarded, so the monitor context in the occurrence event carries the raw ScheduleType integer and the get_schedule_type_display() call is dead.

The described input cannot arrive: all three mark_failed callers pass a check-in whose status is ERROR, TIMEOUT, or MISSED (monitor_consumer.py:877, clock_tasks/check_timeout.py:106-124, clock_tasks/check_missed.py:170), and that check-in is always present in previous_checkins (either constructed directly or as the newest row of the date_added__lte slice), so status_counts is never empty. The docstring's "generic fallback" it cites also does not exist as a code path (see c005).

Grepping for "logger" in all three modules returns only the three getLogger assignments and no call sites, so the split duplicated an already-dead logger into two new files (mark_failed.py:11 keeps its own, also unused).

tests/sentry/monitors/logic/ contains only test_mark_failed.py and test_mark_ok.py; every test of the extracted incident/occurrence logic (threshold behaviour, muting, kafka occurrences, assignment) still lives in test_mark_failed.py, which no longer names what it covers.

Line 146 is exactly SINGULAR_HUMAN_FAILURE_MAP[list(status_counts.keys())[0]]; it materialises the whole key view to take one element, where next(iter(status_counts)) is the idiomatic form. Style-only, but accurate.
Line 132 of the new file is the docstring line containing "humam"; the cited line number matches the file exactly.
